title: Chemistry of Household & Personal Care Products

competencies.text: Construct a table using product labels (bleach, detergents, baking powder, shampoo, soap, toothpaste).
Explain benefits and risks of household products by referring to DTI, FDA, and DENR guidelines.

days.title: Chemistry in Your Cabinet
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to identify the active chemical ingredients in common household products, explain their benefits and risks, and apply DTI, FDA, and DENR guidelines for safe use and disposal.

🏠 Chemistry Is Everywhere at Home

Every product in your kitchen, bathroom, and laundry area is a chemical formulation. Understanding what's inside them helps you use them safely and dispose of them responsibly.

🧴 Common Household Products & Their Chemistry

ProductActive Ingredient(s)Function
BleachSodium hypochlorite (NaClO)Kills germs, whitens fabrics, disinfects surfaces
DetergentSodium lauryl sulfate, surfactants, buildersRemoves grease and dirt from fabrics and dishes
Baking powderSodium bicarbonate + acid (cream of tartar)Releases CO₂ gas to make baked goods rise
ShampooSurfactants, conditioners, preservativesCleans hair and scalp
SoapSodium or potassium salts of fatty acidsDissolves oils and dirt for handwashing
ToothpasteFluoride, abrasives, humectantsCleans teeth, prevents cavities

⚠️ Benefits vs Risks

ProductBenefitRisk if Misused
BleachDisinfects, whitensToxic fumes if mixed with ammonia or acid; skin irritation
DetergentRemoves greaseSkin irritation; harms aquatic life if dumped in rivers
Baking powderMakes food riseSafe in normal use; excess can cause salty taste
ShampooCleans hairEye irritation; some ingredients may cause allergies
SoapKills germsSlips and falls; can dry skin with overuse
ToothpastePrevents cavitiesExcess fluoride (if swallowed) can discolor teeth in children

🏛️ Regulatory Agencies

  • DTI (Department of Trade and Industry): Regulates product labeling, safety standards, and consumer protection. Ensures products carry accurate information.
  • FDA Philippines (Food and Drug Administration): Approves cosmetics, drugs, and personal care products before they can be sold. Monitors adverse reactions.
  • DENR (Department of Environment and Natural Resources): Regulates how chemicals are disposed of to protect the environment. Sets limits on effluent discharge.

🏷️ Reading Product Labels

A proper product label should show:

  • Product name and brand
  • Active ingredients and their concentrations
  • Directions for use
  • Warnings and first-aid instructions
  • Manufacturer details and expiry date
  • FDA registration number (for cosmetics/drugs)

💡 Safe Use & Disposal Practices

  • Never mix bleach with ammonia, vinegar, or other cleaners.
  • Store chemicals out of reach of children, in original containers.
  • Wear gloves when handling strong cleaners.
  • Dispose of chemicals per DENR guidelines — never pour down storm drains.
  • Prefer products with biodegradable or eco-friendly labels.

🌱 Environmental Impact

Detergents with phosphates cause eutrophication in rivers and lakes — harmful algal blooms that kill fish. DENR encourages phosphate-free detergents and bans certain surfactants.

📌 Quick Check

  • What is the active ingredient in bleach? (Answer: sodium hypochlorite)
  • Why should you never mix bleach and ammonia? (Answer: produces toxic chloramine gas)
  • Which agency approves cosmetics in the Philippines? (Answer: FDA Philippines)

days.title: Match Game — Product Ingredients
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each household product or agency to its active ingredient, function, or description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Surfactants that remove grease and dirt
Sodium bicarbonate + acid — releases CO₂ to make baked goods rise
Surfactants and conditioners that clean hair
Sodium salts of fatty acids — dissolves oils and dirt
Approves cosmetics, drugs, and personal care products
Regulates chemical disposal to protect the environment

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Safe Product Use
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🧴 Your helper accidentally mixes bleach with an ammonia-based glass cleaner while cleaning the bathroom. What should she do immediately?

choices.label: A) Add more bleach to neutralize the mixture
B) Leave the room, open windows, and ventilate — the mixture releases toxic chloramine gas
C) Drink water to counteract the fumes

scenario.text: 🍰 A baker wants her cake to rise. Which ingredient is essential?
🌊 Your barangay's river shows a thick green layer of algae. Which household product is MOST likely contributing to this?

choices.label: B) Phosphate-containing laundry detergent dumped into the river

scenario.text: 🛒 You are buying shampoo and see one with an FDA registration number and another without. Which should you choose?

choices.label: A) The cheaper one without a number — labels don't matter
B) The FDA-registered one — it has been checked for safety and quality
C) Neither — all shampoo is unsafe
D) Whichever has the prettiest bottle

scenario.text: ♻️ Your family is cleaning out expired household chemicals. What is the BEST disposal method?

choices.label: A) Pour them down the kitchen sink
B) Throw them in the regular trash
C) Follow DENR guidelines — check with your local barangay for proper hazardous waste disposal
D) Bury them in the backyard

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Household Chem Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Household Chem Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What is the active ingredient in bleach?
Why is it dangerous to mix bleach with ammonia-based cleaners?

choices.label: A) It produces a harmless foam.
B) It releases toxic chloramine gas that can damage lungs.
C) It creates a stronger bleach.

escape.text: Which government agency in the Philippines approves cosmetics and personal care products for sale?
Which agency is responsible for regulating chemical disposal to protect the environment?

choices.label: A) Harmful algal blooms from excess nutrients like phosphates in water
B) A cleaning process for detergents
C) The synthesis of toothpaste ingredients
D) A type of bleaching reaction

escape.text: Which of the following is a BENEFIT of using household chemical products properly?

choices.label: A) They improve hygiene and prevent disease
